content.comment_body: Hello. I recently installed [product_name] [version_no] on my PC after resolving a file issue. Thanks to [user_name] for the updates. Unfortunately, I've already noticed a design change I don't prefer: the color selection for special markers is now fixed to a blue shade, reducing visibility of the black M symbol. Are we moving towards even less customization, like a forced white background? The previous grey worked well for me. I'd like to understand the reasoning behind this design decision. Feeling disappointed.

Hello. I agree with the criticism. I installed [product_name] [version_no] and checked 'What's New'. The welcome screens mention [product_name] [version_no], but there's no information specifically about what has changed in this new version.
Hello [user_name], What you wrote isn't accurate. Information on changes can be found in the Online Help section.

Hello. [user_name], thank you for your response. [user_name], I disagree with your assessment. The critique seems harsh—even if the complaint were correct. My remark is just a perspective on the design changes. There's no poor workmanship here. [product_name] and related products are generally solid, even if I might have chosen differently in some areas.

Hi, Here are some notes about flag colors: Previously, all flags had the same color, which led to confusion when flags with special functions were used as standard flags—resulting in color changes that frustrated users. In [product_name], some flags were given distinct background colors, but not all. Now, each flag with a special function has its own color for clarity, although color preferences will naturally vary among users. It's understandable that not everyone likes the chosen dark blue with black text combination. Regards.

Hello [user_name], Thanks for your reply. In previous versions of [product_name], users could change the color of special markers, with the default being yellow, matching other blocks. Changing the color required knowing about an option in the settings. The current blue and black design is less visually appealing. Cheers.

Update: Here is an example of how the special markers now look, each with distinct colors. This concept is appealing, but the dark blue marker still doesn't look ideal. For comparison, the light blue M1 reflects the color I set in options for regular blocks, which are commonly yellow.

The reason for this change is that each flag now specifically indicates a unique feature for its flag number. Colors were assigned depending on the flag's special function, such as display background controls. For functions without a dedicated color, dark blue was chosen—while not perfect, it highlights that something is different about that particular flag. Personally, I find this approach reasonable.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unhappy with the removal of options to customize special marker colors in the new [product_name] software version. The mandatory dark blue color with black text impairs visibility and overall satisfaction. There's concern about reduced control over visual settings and a lack of clear guidance on features and design changes, affecting user experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to regain the ability to change special marker colors and have control over visual elements within the software for clarity and personal preference.
